statement: Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral. Diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ meet at point $P$. The inradii of triangles $ABP$, $BCP$, $CDP$, and $DAP$ are equal. Prove that $ABCD$ is a rhombus.
Find all integers $n > 1$ with the following property: for all $k$ with $0 \\leq k < n$, there exists a multiple of $n$ whose digit sum leaves a remainder of $k$ when divided by $n$.

Let $N$ be an integer, $N > 2$. Arnold and Bernold play the following game: there are initially $N$ tokens in a pile. Arnold plays first and removes $k$ tokens, $1 \\leq k < N$. Then Bernold removes $m$ tokens, $1 \\leq m \\leq 2k$, and so on — each player removes between $1$ and twice the number of tokens the opponent took last. The player who removes the last token wins. For each value of $N$, determine which player has a winning strategy and describe it.

The infinite sequence $P_0(x), P_1(x), P_2(x), \\ldots$ is defined by $P_0(x) = x$ and $P_n(x) = P_{n-1}(x-1) \\cdot P_{n-1}(x+1)$ for $n \\geq 1$. Find the largest $k$ such that $P_{2014}(x)$ is divisible by $x^k$.

There is an integer in each cell of a $2m \\times 2n$ table. An operation consists of choosing three cells forming an L-tromino (a cell $C$ and two other cells sharing a side with $C$, one horizontally and one vertically) and adding $1$ to each of the three chosen cells. Find a necessary and sufficient condition, in terms of $m$, $n$, and the initial numbers in the table, for a sequence of operations to make all numbers equal.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with incenter $I$ and incircle $\\omega$. Circle $\\omega_A$ is externally tangent to $\\omega$ and tangent to sides $AB$ and $AC$ at $A_1$ and $A_2$, respectively. Let $r_A$ be the line $A_1A_2$. Define $r_B$ and $r_C$ similarly. Lines $r_A$, $r_B$, $r_C$ determine a triangle $XYZ$. Prove that the incenter of $XYZ$, the circumcenter of $XYZ$, and $I$ are collinear.
